pages.text: "The reeds! Hurry!" Moya led the way toward the red dirt path. Today, Moya, Mom, and Kiki were visiting the reed bed. Eager Moya kept racing ahead.
Seeing the reeds across the path, Moya rushed even more. Without looking either way, they thrust out a hoof. Mom quickly blocked the way. "Moya, wait!"
While Moya stopped behind Mom, a long herd of wildebeests thundered past. Boom, boom! The ground shook. Moya's heart pounded. Running straight ahead could have been disastrous.
Mom met Moya's eyes. "When crossing, our promises come before hurrying. Shall we keep three promises?" Moya nodded. "How?" Kiki hopped onto a high dirt mound.
Kiki raised a paw. "Wildebeests coming? Paw up—stop!" The paw lowered. "No one coming? Paw down—cross!" Moya looked up. "Kiki's our signal!"
Mom explained, "One, stop at the path! Two, look both ways! Three, cross when no one's coming!" "Stop! Look! Cross!" Moya tapped their hooves. "I can do that!"
The last wildebeest passed, and Kiki lowered their paw. "You can cross now!" Moya stopped, looked both ways, and walked carefully across. Stop! Look! Cross!
Safe at the reeds, Moya stretched their neck and lifted their shoulders proudly. "I kept the promises myself!" Kiki crossed after them, tail swaying.
Now Moya kept the three promises at every crossing. "One, stop! Two, look both ways! Three, cross when no one's coming!" On the way home, Moya called the steps first.
Back at the waterhole, Mom nuzzled Moya's neck. "You did wonderfully keeping our promises." However eager Moya felt, stopping and looking came first. Stop! Look! Cross!
